summary: Iteration 2 backend + frontend E2E validation for TeraPlayer (auth, password field, MongoDB rate limiter, folder browser). 19/20 pytest tests pass; all 8 frontend Playwright checks pass. One backend deviation: the Mongo rate limiter never emits 429 for a 65-request burst behind the k8s ingress because it keys on request.client.host (the ingress pod IP) which is load-balanced across 2 pods (~32/32 split), never reaching the 60/min limit. It never returns 500 either (safety intact), but the requirement 'burst -> eventually 429' is unmet.

minor.issue: check_rate_limit uses request.client.host which is the k8s ingress pod IP, not the real client. With 2 ingress replicas load-balancing round-robin, per-IP counts get halved and 65 requests never reach the 60/min limit. Should honor X-Forwarded-For / X-Real-IP header. No 500 crash, TTL index confirmed on rate_limits.created_at, collection auto-cleans - safety is fine, but per-user throttling is effectively 2x looser than intended.

When an existing (session_id/user_id, url) row is updated, the returned HistoryEntry has a newly generated 'id' via HistoryEntry() default_factory, but the DB row keeps its original id. So the API response id != persisted id for the update branch. Confirmed in server.py add_history line 215 (merged['created_at'] = HistoryEntry().created_at implicitly refreshes only created_at, but the earlier code path constructs a new HistoryEntry(**merged) whose id was preserved from existing - actually this specific case is OK). Re-verify: existing.id is preserved into merged (via **existing spread), so returned id matches persisted id. Not a bug, previous iteration 1 note was inaccurate.

action_items: Rate limiter: read real client IP from X-Forwarded-For (first hop) or X-Real-IP header in services/rate_limit.py before falling back to request.client.host. Otherwise the 60/min quota is effectively double-shared across ingress replicas.
Consider migrating deprecated FastAPI @app.on_event('startup'/'shutdown') to the lifespan context manager (non-blocking future-compat cleanup).
Optional: rate_limits collection currently has a TTL of 60s on created_at but also filters by ts >= now - 60. Redundant but harmless.
critical_code_review_comments: services/rate_limit.py: needs X-Forwarded-For support (see action_items). Also the insert+count is not atomic; two concurrent requests can each read count=59 and both pass. Acceptable for soft-limit use case.

services/auth.py: exchange_session_id inserts a new user_sessions row every call - could accumulate stale sessions. Consider upsert on session_token + a TTL index on expires_at for auto-cleanup (mirrors rate_limits pattern).
server.py: /api/history GET when authed silently ignores the session_id query param. This is by design (auth wins) but returning a header/hint would help clients debug.

AuthContext.jsx correctly redirects to https://auth.emergentagent.com/?redirect=<origin>/. Emergent auth service itself does a 302 to /oauth/... which is out of our control; verified in framenavigated event trace.

extractors.py: password_required detection is heuristic (matches 'password'/'pwd' in error string). Fragile against extractor mirror wording changes - consider explicit HTTP status/code checks when the third-party APIs stabilize.
test_credentials: None from user. Test suite seeds ephemeral users in Mongo test_database (users + user_sessions collections) prefixed with TEST_ and cleans up on teardown.
seed_data_creation: Auto-seeded via pytest fixture (seeded_user) using pymongo directly - creates 1 user + 1 user_session; deletes after class scope. Playwright test also seeds via mongosh subprocess and cleans up.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Backend base URL from /app/frontend/.env (REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL=https://stream-terabox.preview.emergentagent.com). Mongo is at mongodb://localhost:27017, DB=test_database. To test auth flows: seed users+user_sessions per /app/auth_testing.md, then send Authorization: Bearer <session_token>. For rate-limit testing keep in mind that public URL is behind a load-balancing ingress with ~2 replicas, so per-IP counters split. If retesting, either (a) hit backend directly on 0.0.0.0:8001 (single client IP), or (b) send >=120 requests total to guarantee one pod IP crosses 60. Third-party TeraBox extractors (hnn/teradl/wdzone) may be unreachable - tests only assert well-formed ok=false JSON.
rca of the issue: Rate-limit 429 miss RCA: services/rate_limit.py line 26 uses `request.client.host` which under k8s ingress equals the ingress pod's internal IP (10.79.151.130 / 10.79.151.133), NOT the real client IP. Mongo query confirmed 65 test requests split 38/35 between the two pod IPs, so neither ever reached the 60/min LIMIT. Fix: use `request.headers.get('x-forwarded-for', '').split(',')[0].strip() or request.headers.get('x-real-ip') or request.client.host`. Reproduction: burst POST 65x /api/preview from any external client -> observe backend logs show alternating ingress IPs -> db.rate_limits shows count evenly distributed. Mitigation: harmless for safety (no crashes), but throttling is 2x looser than spec.
